meta.audience: Lachoneus, and then the whole people
meta.location: Zarahemla, and the gathering ground toward Bountiful
meta.unit: The signs and the robber wars (3 Nephi 1–7)
principles: A demand written in the language of courtesy
A defense that refuses to go out
A whole people moved to one ground

world_behind.title: The robbers have a government
world_behind.text: Verse 1 calls Giddianhi their leader and governor. Helaman 6:38 and 39 had the band obtain the sole management of the Nephite government forty years earlier; by this chapter it has a governor of its own, outside the country, writing to Zarahemla as one head of state to another.

world_behind.title: The letter is formally polite
world_behind.text: Verses 2 through 5 praise Lachoneus, his people, and their courage before making any demand. Alma 54 preserves the only other pair of letters between opposing commanders in the record, and neither Moroni nor Ammoron opens with a compliment.

world_behind.title: The offer is partnership
world_behind.text: Verse 7 asks them to yield, take up the secret works, and share the spoil as brethren. Helaman 6:21 and 22 record the more part of the Nephites accepting exactly that offer a generation earlier, so the governor knows what saying yes to it looks like.

world_behind.title: Giddianhi claims the works are good and old
world_behind.text: Verse 9 says he knows the society and its works to be good and of ancient date. Helaman 6:26 and 27 answer the antiquity claim directly: the oaths did not come from any record but were put into Gadianton's heart by the being who plotted with Cain.

world_behind.title: The grievance is invented
world_behind.text: Verse 11 has Mormon noting that the wrongs to be avenged were suffered by men who had wronged themselves by dissenting.

world_behind.title: Chief captains were normally prophets
world_behind.text: Verse 19 gives it as the Nephite custom, kept except in times of wickedness, and says Gidgiddoni and the chief judge were both prophets.

world_behind.title: The whole nation relocates
world_behind.text: Verses 22 through 24 have them moving with herds, grain, and substance into one block of land running from Zarahemla to the line between Bountiful and Desolation. Alma 22:32 measures that line at a day and a half's journey, so a whole nation is being packed into a strip of that width.

words.text: Not able to be defeated. The record uses the word twice, at Alma 52:33 of Teancum's men and here of the robbers, and the King James Bible never. Giddianhi applies it to his own troops as an argument.
An organized body with members. The record uses the word four times, twice of the Jaredite combinations in Ether. Verse 9 is where the Gadianton band names itself.
Confident forwardness. It appears twelve times in the record, and the King James Bible ten. Verse 11 uses it of Giddianhi's demand, and 3 Nephi 4:14 uses it of how he fought and died.
In no way at all. The record uses the word eleven times and the King James Bible never. Lachoneus attaches it to the one condition of deliverance.
Highest in rank. The word turns up twice, both in this book, here, and the King James Bible eight times. Verse 18 stacks it with "great commander" to place Gidgiddoni.
Small shields carried on the arm. The word occurs once in the record and five times in the King James Bible. Verse 26 lists it last, after armor and shields.

phrases.term: Lachoneus, most noble and chief governor of the land
phrases.text: The salutation of a formal epistle. Acts 24:3 addresses a Roman governor the same way.

phrases.term: As if ye were supported by the hand of a god
phrases.text: Praise with the claim hollowed out. Giddianhi grants the appearance and declines the substance in one clause.

phrases.term: That which ye do call so
phrases.text: The tell at the end of the compliment. Their liberty, property, and country are named and then bracketed as things they merely call by those names.

phrases.term: Become acquainted with our secret works, and become our brethren
phrases.text: The terms of surrender are initiation. Membership in the society is the price and the promise together.

phrases.term: Which society and the works thereof I know to be good
phrases.text: Giddianhi's own assessment, stated without argument. Verse 9 adds that the works are of ancient date and were handed down.

phrases.term: Avenging the wrongs of those that had received no wrong
phrases.text: Mormon's judgment on the grievance. He grants that they were wronged and says they did it to themselves.

phrases.term: He did cause that his people should cry unto the Lord for strength
phrases.text: The governor's first act after refusing. Hezekiah does the same thing with Sennacherib's letter in 2 Kings 19:14.

phrases.term: Except ye repent of all your iniquities, and cry unto the Lord, ye will in nowise be delivered
phrases.text: A military proclamation with a moral condition. Lachoneus makes repentance part of the defense plan.

phrases.term: It was the custom among all the Nephites to appoint for their chief captains... some one that had the spirit of revelation
phrases.text: The staffing rule stated as national practice. The parenthesis notes it lapsed in times of wickedness.

phrases.term: We will wait till they shall come against us
phrases.text: Gidgiddoni's answer to a proposal to attack. Alma 43:46 had given the rule about not striking first, and this is a commander applying it.

phrases.term: They did dwell in one land, and in one body
phrases.text: The result of the gathering. A dispersed nation becomes a single concentrated target that cannot be picked apart.

verses.label: v. 2–10
verses.title: Nine verses in the enemy's own hand
verses.text: The record reproduces the robber chief's letter entire and does not interrupt it. Your stands sixteen times in this chapter and every use falls inside the letter, in five verses: your firmness, your cities, your lands, your possessions. Nothing is paraphrased and no comment is inserted until verse 11, which reports only Lachoneus's reaction. A document written to destroy the Nephite state is preserved in the Nephite record at greater length than the reply to it, which is never quoted at all.

verses.label: v. 8
verses.title: One formula for the promise and the threat
verses.text: The record preserves an oath sworn twice over in matched halves: "I swear unto you, if ye will do this, with an oath, ye shall not be destroyed; but if ye will not do this, I swear unto you with an oath, that on the morrow month I will command that my armies shall come down against you." Same verb, same object, opposite conditions. The construction gives surrender and annihilation the identical grammatical weight, which is the whole argument of the letter, stated once and then reversed.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: The claim the record cannot easily deny
verses.text: Giddianhi describes his society in his own words: "which society and the works thereof I know to be good; and they are of ancient date and they have been handed down unto us." The first clause is a robber's opinion. The second and third are claims about history, and the volume has already agreed with them. Hel. 6:26–30 traces the same oaths back through Gadianton to Cain and calls their transmission a handing down. An enemy's boast about antiquity is left standing because the record's own account of the matter says the same thing.

verses.label: v. 19
verses.title: A custom, with its exception in brackets
verses.text: The appointment of a commander comes with a rule, and the rule comes with a qualifier the record puts in parentheses: "it was the custom among all the Nephites to appoint for their chief captains, (save it were in their times of wickedness) some one that had the spirit of revelation and also prophecy." The bracket is doing the work. It concedes that the custom lapsed, and it tells a reader how to read every earlier chapter where a commander was appointed without any mention of revelation.

verses.label: v. 20–21
verses.title: A general refuses the attack
verses.text: The people ask for an offensive, "let us go up upon the mountains and into the wilderness, that we may fall upon the robbers and destroy them in their own lands." Gidgiddoni answers with a prohibition and a reason: "The Lord forbid; for if we should go up against them the Lord would deliver us into their hands; therefore we will prepare ourselves in the center of our lands." The exchange is preserved as speech on both sides, and the refusal is not tactical. A commander who has just been introduced as a man with the spirit of prophecy declines the popular plan on grounds no soldier could verify.

verses.label: v. 22–25
verses.title: A nation gathered into one place
verses.text: The result of the proclamation is stated with unusual geographic precision: the land appointed is Zarahemla and the ground "between the land Zarahemla and the land Bountiful, yea, to the line which was between the land Bountiful and the land Desolation." Then the state of the people is put in a phrase the volume uses for nothing else: "they did dwell in one land, and in one body." Seven years of grain and provisions are carried in with them. The defensive plan is total, and its cost is that everything the Nephites own is now in one place.

chapter.title: The threat arrives in courteous form
chapter.text: Ten verses of praise, sympathy, and reasonableness carry a demand for the whole country. The style is the point.

chapter.title: Giddianhi cannot help qualifying
chapter.text: Verse 2 calls their liberty and country "that which ye do call so." The contempt shows through the compliment.

chapter.title: Surrender is offered as membership
chapter.text: Verse 7 promises partnership and the secret works. What is on offer is not mercy but recruitment into the society.

chapter.title: The band claims antiquity as authority
chapter.text: Verse 9 says the works are of ancient date and handed down. Helaman 6:26 had already traced that descent and named its source.

chapter.title: The governor does not reply
chapter.text: Verse 12 says he did not hearken to the epistle. His answer is a proclamation to his own people rather than a letter back.

chapter.title: Repentance is written into the defense order
chapter.text: Verse 15 makes it a condition of deliverance in the same document that organizes the fortifications.

chapter.title: The people want to attack and are refused
chapter.text: Verses 20 and 21 have Gidgiddoni citing the Lord against a preemptive campaign. The discipline of Alma 43:46 is still operating.

chapter.title: A nation makes itself one target on purpose
chapter.text: Verse 25 has them dwelling in one land and one body. Concentration is the plan, and 3 Nephi 4 will show why it worked.

applications.title: Read past the courtesy
applications.text: The letter flattered before it demanded, and slipped its real view into a subordinate clause. Notice what a polite message assumes about you.

applications.title: Notice the offer to make you an insider
applications.text: Giddianhi promised they would not be slaves but brethren and partners of all his substance. The most effective recruiting does not demand submission; it offers belonging, which is why it reaches people who would have refused an order.

applications.title: Watch confidence being used as a credential
applications.text: Giddianhi writes that the society is good and that it is of ancient date, and offers nothing further. Age and certainty are the two supports the sentence offers, and neither is a reason.

applications.title: Do not answer on the terms offered
applications.text: Lachoneus never replied. Refusing to enter someone else's frame is sometimes the whole of a good response.

applications.title: Put the moral condition in the operational plan
applications.text: The same proclamation that ordered fortifications called for repentance. Treating those as one task rather than two is the chapter's method.

applications.title: Choose leaders by what they listen to
applications.text: The Nephite custom was to appoint chief captains who had the spirit of revelation and prophecy, and the verse puts the exception in a parenthesis: except in their times of wickedness. What a people uses as its selection test tells you what kind of season it is in.

applications.title: Concentrate rather than chase
applications.text: They were told not to go hunting in the mountains. Defending well from your own ground beats pursuing on the enemy's.

applications.title: Gather where the ground is still good
applications.text: Lachoneus concentrated everyone in the land southward because of the great curse upon the land northward. When you consolidate, the choice of where does as much work as the decision to consolidate at all.

questions.text: Whose flattery have I accepted without hearing the clause at the end?
What has been offered to me that would cost me my independence?
What do I call good because it is old and was handed to me?
Whose grievance have I taken up without checking it?
What am I answering that I should simply decline to engage?
Where am I chasing a problem onto ground I cannot hold?
What would it look like to gather my life into one body?
